articles.title: Reviving a 200-year-old IPA recipe first made in a teapot in 1822
articles.summary: Jamie Allsopp helps revive a recipe created in 1822 after it is found with other beer recipes in an attic.
articles.body:
The descendant of a brewer who made the first commercially successful India Pale Ale (IPA) has revived his seven-times-great-grandfather's recipe.

Samuel Allsopp created the beer in a teapot in 1822 after being challenged to make one which would last the six-month sea journey to India.

Allsopp went on to help establish Burton-upon-Trent, Staffordshire, as the world's brewing capital.

Steve Holt, owner of Kirkstall Brewery in Leeds, found the leather-bound brewery ledger containing the recipe and teamed up with Allsopp's descendent Jamie Allsopp to remake what they called "one of the most important beers in brewing history."

Jamie said: "It started off the craft beer revolution. I'm really looking forward to drinking it with publicans and customers. It's going to be fantastic."

Allsopp's India Pale Ale was released in 70 pubs across the country on Friday, including Burton Bridge Inn and The Roebuck Inn, returning the beer to its original hometown.

In the year it was first released, the trade in sending beer to India was dominated by London brewer George Hodgson, but pale ale had become unreliable and unable to make the journey unspoiled.

'Now feels right to show Banks's vital history'

Beer boom goes flat as breweries call last orders

New beer tribute to city's 'rich brewing history'

Jamie, a ninth-generation family member, resurrected Allsopp's in 2021.

Recalling the IPA's history, he told the BBC: "Samuel was asked by the East India Company to brew a beer that would last the arduous six-month journey to India, as all other beers were arriving in bad condition.

"Samuel Allsopp did something hitherto unknown, he upped the alcohol and hop content which both act as preservatives.

"It really dialled it up strongly, and it was a really bitter beer. At the time it wouldn't have been drinkable straight out of the brewery, but after the six months at sea going down the Cape of Good Hope, it mellowed and arrived in India in really good condition."

This journey formed the humble beginnings of the popular ale. To save time and ingredients, Samuel and his head maltster, Job Goodhead, used a teapot to brew the first IPA and helped pioneer a new taste.

After growing into what has been described as one of Britain's great brewing empires, Allsopp's fortunes began to turn and the family lost control of the business in the 1930s.

More than two centuries on, the ledger containing over 100 handwritten recipes, including IPA, Pale Ale, Double Diamond, Stout, Arctic Ale and dozens of forgotten brews, was found in an attic in Leeds.

Jamie added: "Without the recipes I wasn't interested in producing guesswork."

He said he was not looking for "historical interpretations of IPA".

"It had to be the real deal – with the right malts, hops, and style that could make our beer revered once again," he said.

"If we can persuade more people to fall in love with cask again, then we've achieved something far bigger than simply bringing back one historic beer."

articles.title: Urnas eletrônicas são substituídas na Baixada Santista no 2º turno | G1
articles.standfirst: Trocas ocorreram em Praia Grande, Guarujá e Santos neste domingo (25). Levantamento feito com as zonas eleitorais também apontou infiltrações e goteiras em Santos, mas sem prejuízo à votação.
articles.summary: Urnas eletrônicas substituídas na Baixada Santista em Santos, Praia Grande e Guarujá por falhas técnicas e goteiras não interrompem o segundo turno.
articles.body:
Urna eletrônica desligada - imagem ilustrativa — Foto: TRE - SP

Urnas eletrônicas foram substituídas durante o 2º turno das eleições, neste domingo (25), na Baixada Santista. Até as 11h30, 12 equipamentos haviam sido trocados em Santos, Praia Grande e Guarujá, segundo levantamento feito pelo g1 diretamente com as zonas eleitorais dos municípios.

As substituições ocorreram por problemas técnicos, incluindo falhas em terminais de mesários e baterias. Apesar das chuvas registradas na região, as zonas eleitorais consultadas não informaram mudanças nos locais de votação provocadas pelo tempo.

Conforme as informações repassadas pelas zonas eleitorais, as oito substituições registradas até as 10h30:

Cinco urnas da 307ª Zona Eleitoral foram substituídas nas escolas municipais Ronaldo Sérgio Alves Lameira, Newtom Almeida de Castro, Carlos Roberto Dias e José Padim Mouta, além da Escola Estadual Vila Tupi. Outra troca ocorreu na 406ª Zona Eleitoral, após problema no terminal do mesário.

Duas substituições foram registradas na 118ª Zona Eleitoral, na Praça Maria Coelho Lopes, sem número, e na Escola Americana, na Rua Rosinha Viegas, 55, na Encruzilhada.

Outras duas trocas ocorreram na 273ª Zona Eleitoral, na Escola Anália Franco, na Avenida Ana Costa, 277, no Gonzaga, e na Escola Estadual Professor Primo Ferreira, na Rua Dom Pedro I, 58, na Vila Belmiro. A substituição nesta última unidade foi informada durante uma ronda realizada às 9h30.

Duas urnas haviam sido substituídas na 212ª Zona Eleitoral. Os endereços das ocorrências ainda não haviam sido informados.

Apesar das chuvas que atingiram a Baixada Santista, as zonas eleitorais consultadas não relataram necessidade de mudança dos locais de votação.

Em Santos, a 118ª Zona Eleitoral informou que algumas salas apresentaram infiltrações e goteiras. Segundo o cartório, os problemas não comprometeram a votação, inclusive na Zona Noroeste.

Bertioga: nenhuma ocorrência registrada.

Itanhaém: nenhuma ocorrência registrada.

Mongaguá: nenhuma ocorrência registrada.

Peruíbe: nenhuma urna quebrada ou substituída.

São Vicente: a 177ª Zona Eleitoral não registrou ocorrências. A 340ª não respondeu à nova consulta, mas havia informado anteriormente que não registrava problemas.

O g1 também procurou a zona eleitoral responsável por Cubatão, mas não teve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: Conheça cidade do TO onde Lula e Flávio  empataram no 1º turno | G1
articles.standfirst: Os dois candidatos à presidência terminaram o primeiro turno com a mesma votação em Crixás. Cada um recebeu 47,75% dos votos válidos, o equivalente a 679 votos.
articles.summary: Os dois candidatos à presidência terminaram o primeiro turno com a mesma votação em Crixás. Cada um recebeu 47,75% dos votos válidos, o equivalente a 679 votos.
articles.body:
Crixás do Tocantins, na região sul do estado, foi uma das duas cidades do país onde Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) empataram no primeiro turno. A outra foi Trabiju, no interior de São Paulo

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

Os dois candidatos à presidência terminaram o primeiro turno com a mesma votação em Crixás. Cada um recebeu 47,75% dos votos válidos, o equivalente a 679 votos. Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) ficou em terceiro lugar, com 2,25% (32 votos), seguido por Augusto Cury (Avante), com 1,62% (23 votos); Renan Santos (Missão), com 0,56% (8 votos); e Samara (UP), com 0,07% (1 voto).

Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) em agendas eleitorais na reta final da eleição — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert / Vitor Salles

Com 1.470 habitantes, segundo o Censo 2022 do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), Crixás do Tocantins está entre os municípios menos populosos do país.

Crixás do Tocantins, no sul do estado — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Crixás

O g1 conversou com a prefeita Ana Flávia (Republicanos), conhecida como Flávia do Leitoa, que está no segundo mandato. Segundo ela, nunca havia ocorrido um empate entre candidatos à presidência no município.

“Foi a primeira vez. Acredito que não teremos um novo empate, mas quem ganhar vai ser por diferença mínima”, afirmou.

A prefeita disse que ficou surpresa com o resultado e explicou que decidiu não declarar apoio a nenhum dos candidatos para respeitar as diferentes posições políticas dos moradores.

“Eu não esperava esse empate, fiquei surpresa. Eu não declarei apoio por respeito, porque temos gente que vota em Lula e também no Flávio Bolsonaro. Então, não declaramos apoio”, explicou.

Cidade fica na região sul — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Crixás

Segundo a prefeitura, Crixás do Tocantins foi elevado à categoria de município pela Lei Estadual nº 680, de 26 de maio de 1994, e instalado em 1º de janeiro de 1997, após ser desmembrado de Aliança do Tocantins. O nome faz referência ao Rio Crixás, e o complemento “do Tocantins” foi adotado para diferenciar o município de Crixás, em Goiás, que já existia na época.

A economia do município tem como base a agricultura, com destaque para o cultivo de soja e milho. Crixás do Tocantins tem área territorial de 983,766 km², conforme o IBGE.

Ana Flávia foi eleita prefeita pela primeira vez em 2020. Em 2024, foi reeleita para o segundo mandato, desta vez sem concorrentes.

articles.title: Alan Rick (Republicanos) vota em Rio Branco | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato ao governo do Acre votou neste domingo (25) na Escola Técnica em Saúde Maria Moreira da Rocha.
articles.summary: Candidato ao governo do Acre votou neste domingo (25) na Escola Técnica em Saúde Maria Moreira da Rocha.
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo do Acre Alan Rick ( Republicanos ) votou neste domingo (25) na Escola Técnica em Saúde Maria Moreira da Rocha, em Rio Branco.

Ele chegou ao local de votação por volta de 8h40 (horário oficial do estado), acompanhado da senadora eleita Mara Rocha (Republicanos), do candidato a vice Ricardo Leite (Republicanos), além da esposa, do filho e de demais apoiadores.

Após votar, Alan falou que este segundo turno é diferente e classificou como 'difícil'. Ao avaliar as últimas semanas, disse que foi uma campanha 'pé no chão' e que respeita o resultado das urnas, independente do resultado.

"Enfrentamos uma máquina poderosa, usada ostensivamente contra nós, mas o importante é que nós recebemos o abraço do povo, o carinho da população e isso vai ficar guardado no meu coração. Seja qual for o resultado das urnas, eu espero que seja a nossa vitória, eu saio muito feliz", falou.

Eleições 2026 - Rio Branco (AC): Alan Rick (Republicanos) vota em Rio Branco — Foto: Jhenyfer de Souza/g1

O tempo de permanência do candidato no local foi de cerca de 20 minutos, onde cumprimentou apoiadores e falou com a imprensa sobre as expectativas após o término da votação.

"Se Deus quiser [teremos] uma vitória, nós vamos honrar o nosso Acre, trabalhar por esse povo amado do nosso estado sofrido, que precisa de um governo que realmente atenda as suas necessidades", finalizou.

Eleições 2026 - Rio Branco (AC): Alan Rick (Republicanos) chegou ao local de votação com esposa, filho e senadora eleita Mara Rocha (Republicanos) — Foto: Jhenyfer de Souza/g1

articles.title: Governador reeleito do Piauí, Rafael Fonteles vota em Teresina | G1
articles.standfirst: Governador afirmou estar otimista com o resultado do segundo turno e acompanhará a apuração ao lado de Lula, em São Paulo.
articles.summary: Governador afirmou estar otimista com o resultado do segundo turno e acompanhará a apuração ao lado de Lula, em São Paulo.
articles.body:
O governador Rafael Fonteles (PT) votou, neste domingo (25), no Colégio Madre Savina, na Zona Leste de Teresina e estar confiante com a reeleição do presidente Lula (PT).

Rafael comentou sobre a participação na coordenação de campanha do segundo turno de Lula (PT) e confirmou que vai acompanhar a apuração do resultado ao lado do candidato à reeleição, em São Paulo.

"Eu dei uma modesta contribuição nesse segundo turno, sobretudo chamando mais atenção na importância das redes sociais no processo de comunicação social e política. Eu acredito que ele melhorou muito", comentou.

O governador chegou ao local de votação por volta de 10h30, acompanhado da esposa.

articles.title: Assédio eleitoral no trabalho: como denunciar no 2º turno no PA | G1
articles.standfirst: Tribunal Regional do Trabalho (TRT-8) mantém plantão até a manhã da segunda-feira (26). Denúncia pode ser feita de forma anônima e online.
articles.summary: Assédio eleitoral no trabalho pode ser denunciado anonimamente ao MPT no Pará, com plantão do TRT-8 disponível até segunda-feira para proteger o direito ao voto.
articles.body:
TRT faz campanha contra assédio eleitoral; — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

A Justiça do Trabalho do Pará e do Amapá segue com o Plantão do Judiciário no combate ao assédio eleitoral no ambiente de trabalho durante o segundo turno das eleições.

Os trabalhos começaram na sexta-feira (23), às 15h01, e seguem até esta segunda-feira (26), às 7h59, com juízes do 1º Grau e desembargadores no 2º Grau.

O desembargador do TRT-8 Francisco Sérgio Silva Rocha alerta sobre o momento de polarização vivido na sociedade brasileira e o reflexo dele nas eleições.

"O assédio eleitoral na relação de trabalho pode acontecer por vários fatores. Pode acontecer diretamente com uma propaganda direta do empregador em face do empregado, pedindo para que ele vote em determinado candidato ou deixe de votar em determinado candidato", exemplifica.

"[O assédio eleitoral] pode assumir feições indiretas como propaganda no local de trabalho, incentivo da visita de candidatos da preferência do empregador ao local de trabalho, palestras e até o uso de notícias falsas para implantar um receio ou um favorecimento a determinado candidato."

Também configura assédio ameaçar, demitir ou retirar benefícios de um funcionário por causa do voto.

Segundo o desembargador, a conduta gera consequências nas duas esferas: "Porque além disso ser crime eleitoral, existe uma grave irregularidade trabalhista passível de reparação. O empregador, e assim se der, ele está sujeito não só à sua responsabilização perante os órgãos eleitorais, mas também à sua responsabilização perante os órgãos, seja de fiscalização do trabalho, seja nos órgãos jurisdicionais de proteção do trabalho."

"A existência deste procedimento implica numa falta grave cometida pelo empregador, que pode dar direito ao empregado, inclusive, de pleitear a sua rescisão do contrato de trabalho de forma indireta, além de dano moral por conta do comportamento do empregador", pontua.

A Justiça do Trabalho atua em conjunto com a Justiça Eleitoral, o Ministério Público do Trabalho e o Ministério Público Eleitoral para prevenir e reparar casos.

O trabalhador pode recorrer aos órgãos competentes. Quaisquer provas são admitidas, conversas de WhatsApp, prints, fotografias, depoimentos de outros trabalhadores, tudo isso pode auxiliar o trabalhador para comprovar o assédio eleitoral.

Denúncias podem ser feitas via Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT), pelo site do órgão . O trabalhador não precisa se identificar: a denúncia pode ser anônima. Basta apresentar os dados relativos ao assédio no site do Ministério Público do Trabalho. A partir daí, o próprio MPT faz a investigação. Se entender que o assédio está configurado, o órgão entra com a ação.

articles.title: Transporte irregular de eleitores: ônibus é apreendido em Alagoas | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o MP, veículo não estava cadastrado na Justiça Eleitoral. Caso era acompanhado por promotora eleitoral.
articles.summary: Veículo contratado por secretário de Paripueira não tinha cadastro na Justiça Eleitoral, configurando transporte irregular de eleitores no segundo turno das Eleições 2026.
articles.body:
Ônibus contratado por secretário é apreendido por transporte irregular de eleitores em AL — Foto: MP/AL

Um ônibus contratado por um secretário municipal de Paripueira , na Região Metropolitana de Maceió , foi apreendido neste domingo (25) após ser flagrado transportando eleitores de forma irregular durante o segundo turno das eleições presidenciais de 2026.

Segundo o Ministério Público de Alagoas (MPAL), o veículo não estava cadastrado na Justiça Eleitoral para realizar o transporte de eleitores, o que motivou a apreensão.

A promotora eleitoral Alexandra Beurlen acompanhava a ocorrência, que seguia em andamento até a última atualização desta reportagem.

De acordo com o MP, o transporte irregular de eleitores pode configurar crime eleitoral. O órgão informou que o ônibus havia sido contratado por um secretário municipal de Paripueira, mas não divulgou a identidade dele.

Até o momento, não haviam sido divulgadas informações sobre a quantidade de eleitores transportados nem se outras pessoas foram levadas para prestar esclarecimentos.

O caso seguia sob acompanhamento do Ministério Público Eleitoral.

articles.title: ‘Entregar todo o poder aos Bolsonaro ou dar última vitória a Lula’: imprensa mundial repercute votação no 2º turno | G1
articles.standfirst: Jornais de todo o mundo reportaram sobre a disputa derradeira entre o presidente Lula e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro neste domingo (25) e destacaram a importância que o resultado do pleito terá para a América Latina e para o mundo.
articles.summary: Jornais de todo o mundo reportaram sobre a disputa derradeira entre o presidente Lula e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro neste domingo (25) e destacaram a importância que o resultado do pleito terá para a América Latina e para o mundo.
articles.body:
Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) em agendas eleitorais na reta final da eleição — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert / Vitor Salles

A imprensa internacional repercutiu neste domingo (25) a votação no 2º turno das eleições presidenciais brasileiras, disputado entre os candidatos Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).

As manchetes destacaram a importância que o resultado do pleito no Brasil terá para a América Latina e para o mundo. Veja abaixo.

O El País , da Espanha, afirmou que o Brasil decidirá entre "entregar todo o poder aos Bolsonaro ou dar uma última vitória a Lula";

A Associated Press , dos Estados Unidos , chamou de "decisão tensa" a votação deste domingo;

O New York Times , dos Estados Unidos, afirmou que "Flávio pode conseguir a maior vitória da direita da América Latina";

O The Guardian , do Reino Unido, disse que o resultado da eleição é "altamente imprevisível".

Reportagem do jornal El País, da Espanha, sobre a votação no 2º turno das eleições presidenciais brasileiras em 25 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/El País

O El País, da Espanha, afirmou que o Brasil decidirá entre "entregar todo o poder aos Bolsonaro ou dar uma última vitória a Lula".

A fala é uma alusão ao fato do Congresso brasileiro ter se tornado mais conservador após o 1º turno, com uma expansão da bancada do PL, que agora é o partido com a maior bancada em ambas as casas legislativas.

Eleger o senador Flávio Bolsonaro, herdeiro de um golpista e de uma dinastia ultraconservadora que engoliu a direita tradicional, significa transformá-lo no presidente mais poderoso das últimas décadas, porque ele comandaria o governo federal, controlaria o Congresso com uma maioria recorde e moldaria o Supremo Tribunal Federal", escreveu.

O jornal disse ainda que uma vitória de Lula significaria "manter o rumo político e econômico, apostar, nestes tempos tão turbulentos, em um mundo regido por regras e em um líder com credenciais democráticas consolidadas".

A reportagem disse também que "brasileiros de esquerda e direita se mobilizaram em massa nas últimas semanas de campanha em busca dos votos que vão decidir as eleições mais acirradas de suas vidas".

Reportagem da agência de notícias Associated Press, dos Estados Unidos, sobre a votação no 2º turno das eleições presidenciais brasileiras em 25 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/Associated Press

A agência de notícias norte-americana Associated Press deu destaque ao elemento de tensão que cerca a votação deste domingo.

"Brasileiros votam em uma disputa tensa entre Lula e Bolsonaro com influência dos EUA e com a América Latina em jogo. (...) O resultado determinará se os Estados Unidos ampliarão significativamente sua crescente influência na América Latina", afirmou a agência.

A reportagem citou uma pesquisa do Datafolha desta semana que mostrou Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro apareceram com 50% da intenção de voto. Também afirmou que "a diferença entre os dois candidatos é marcante":

" Uma vitória de Bolsonaro representaria uma guinada à direita do país mais populoso e da maior economia da América Latina , em um ano com vitórias de aliados de Trump [na região]. (...) Uma vitória de Lula manteria o Brasil e o México sob a liderança de políticos de centro-esquerda", afirmou.

Reportagem do jornal The New York Times, dos Estados Unidos, sobre a votação no 2º turno das eleições presidenciais brasileiras em 25 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/New York Times

O jornal "The New York Times" afirmou que "Flávio pode conquistar a maior vitória da direita da América Latina" e também repercutiu o quão acirrada está a disputa neste segundo turno.

"Os brasileiros vão às urnas neste domingo para eleger um novo presidente em uma eleição disputada ferozmente [entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro], no que representa o maior teste até agora para a direita em ascensão que vem conquistando presidências em toda a América Latina (...) Uma vitória de Bolsonaro representaria a maior conquista até agora de um movimento de direita em ascensão que avança por toda a América Latina", afirmou a reportagem.

O veículo norte-americano também citou o grande interesse do governo Trump no pleito —o presidente dos EUA tem afinidade ideológica com Flávio.

Reportagem do jornal The Guardian, do Reino Unido, sobre a votação no 2º turno das eleições presidenciais brasileiras em 25 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/The Guardian

O jornal britânico "The Guardian" afirmou que o pleito brasileiro é "altamente imprevisível" e destacou que a distância entre os dois candidatos é a menor da história para um 2º turno na disputa pela presidência.

A reportagem disse que Lula "tenta uma volta por cima sem precedentes" contra Flávio, e citou a "vitória surpreendente" do bolsonarista no 1º turno.

"A diferença entre eles foi a menor já registrada em um primeiro turno, inferior a 2% dos votos. O presidente, de 81 anos, passou boa parte da campanha do segundo turno concentrado em estimular o comparecimento às urnas (...) e em alimentar temores sobre o que significaria o retorno ao poder de um integrante da família Bolsonaro".

O jornal também citou que Flávio pretende dar um indulto a seu pai, Jair Bolsonaro, caso seja eleito e que ele prometeu mudar a Constituição brasileira.

articles.title: Após votar em SP, Tarcísio diz que Flávio Bolsonaro será 'presidente da pacificação' caso vença a eleição | G1
articles.standfirst: Governador compareceu ao Colégio Miguel de Cervantes, no Morumbi, na Zona Sul de São Paulo, neste domingo (25). Aliado do candidato do PL, político foi reeleito no primeiro turno.
articles.summary: Governador compareceu ao Colégio Miguel de Cervantes, no Morumbi, na Zona Sul de São Paulo, neste domingo (25). Aliado do candidato do PL, político foi reeleito no primeiro turno.
articles.body:
O governador reeleito de São Paulo , Tarcísio Gomes de Freitas ( Republicanos ), votou na manhã deste domingo (25), no segundo turno das eleições presidenciais de 2026, no Colégio Miguel de Cervantes, no Morumbi, na Zona Sul da capital paulista. Após votar, ele afirmou que o resultado do primeiro turno representou um "sinal de mudança" e demonstrou confiança na vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ) sobre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ( PT ).

Tarcísio também afirmou que Flávio deverá ser um presidente de pacificação política, com um governo voltado tanto para quem votou nele quanto para quem apoiou o adversário.

"Pode ter certeza que o Flávio vai governar não só para os aliados, mas também para os adversários. Ele vai governar para quem votou nele, para quem não votou nele. Ele vai governar para o Brasil. Ele vai ser um presidente de pacificação dentro disso", declarou.

O governador disse ainda que pretende ajudar Flávio a conduzir a gestão federal, mas ressaltou que a escolha dos ministros cabe ao presidente da República. Segundo ele, a contribuição de aliados e governadores deverá ocorrer ao longo de todo o mandato, por meio de conversas e troca de experiências.

"A nossa missão é ajudar o Flávio a fazer um bom governo. Eu falava ao longo da campanha, falei muito aqui com uma série de pessoas, que a gente não vai ajudar o Flávio a se eleger presidente da República. A gente vai ajudar o Flávio a ser um grande presidente da República", afirmou.

Sobre a formação do ministério, Tarcísio disse que Flávio deverá ter autonomia para escolher sua equipe, assim como ele afirmou fazer em São Paulo. O governador defendeu a escolha de quadros técnicos, sem que a montagem do secretariado seja determinada por acordos partidários.

Tarcísio de Freitas depois de votar — Foto: Marília Barbosa/g1

"É o presidente da República. Eu acho que ele tem que montar a equipe do coração dele, assim como eu faço em São Paulo. Eu monto a equipe do meu coração. Eu procuro os quadros técnicos", disse.

Tarcísio também afirmou que o apoio ao eventual governo de Flávio não ficará restrito ao período eleitoral e que os governadores aliados poderão contribuir com a administração federal ao longo dos próximos anos.

"Então, essa questão de montagem de equipe é uma questão muito do presidente da República. Agora, São Paulo é um estado importante. É o estado de maior PIB do Brasil. A gente representa um terço da nossa economia e a gente abriga 22% da população", declarou.

Ao comentar o resultado do primeiro turno, Tarcísio afirmou que a votação indicou o desejo de mudança de parte do eleitorado brasileiro e disse acreditar que esse movimento será confirmado neste domingo.

"O primeiro turno deu um sinal muito claro para o Brasil, que foi o sinal de mudança. E eu tenho certeza que esse sinal vai ser confirmado agora no segundo turno", afirmou.

O governador, reeleito em 4 de outubro após derrotar Fernando Haddad (PT), criticou o governo Lula e disse que os eleitores estão insatisfeitos com a atual gestão federal.

"A gente tem um voto de indignação, um voto de exaustão, um voto de quem se cansou ao longo desses quatro anos de uma série de promessas não cumpridas, uma série de compromissos que não foram honrados, se cansou de uma equipe que não conseguiu dar respostas", declarou.

Durante a entrevista, Tarcísio relembrou que acompanhou sua primeira eleição presidencial em 1989, quando Lula já disputava a Presidência da República. Ele comparou as transformações tecnológicas das últimas décadas com problemas estruturais que, segundo ele, permanecem sem solução no país.

"A gente saiu da carta para a inteligência artificial. E, no entanto, a gente vem ficando para trás em uma série de parâmetros. Não é possível que o Brasil, nessa altura do campeonato, tenha metade da sua população sem coleta e tratamento de esgoto", disse.

O governador defendeu que o Brasil aproveite oportunidades nas áreas de inteligência artificial, biotecnologia, transição energética e segurança alimentar. Para isso, afirmou que o país precisa de uma equipe de governo mais qualificada.

Tarcísio (Republicanos) vota no Morumbi, Zona Sul de São Paulo — Foto: Marília Barbosa/g1

"A gente precisa de pessoas sérias, de governo sério, de equipe competente. E eu tenho certeza que essa mudança vai vir, começa a partir de hoje, com a eleição de Flávio Bolsonaro presidente", afirmou.

Ao concluir, Tarcísio voltou a manifestar otimismo com a possibilidade de um governo de Flávio Bolsonaro e reforçou a defesa da pacificação política.

"Estou muito otimista com o governo que virá, com uma equipe mais qualificada e com um governo de pacificação. E, sobretudo, o Brasil precisa também de pacificação", concluiu.

Aliado do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL), Tarcísio participou de atos de campanha em apoio a Flávio durante o segundo turno e se colocou à disposição para ajudar na campanha do candidato em São Paulo e em outros estados.

A votação deste domingo começou às 8h e segue até as 17h, pelo horário de Brasília. A divulgação dos resultados terá início após o encerramento da votação.

articles.summary: Corina Machado havia deixado o país sul-americano em dezembro após ter vencido o prêmio Nobel da Paz e passar meses escondida em meio à repressão do governo Maduro. Opositora retornou neste (25) domingo após diversas tentativas frustradas.
articles.body:
A líder da oposição venezuelana, Maria Corina Machado, participa de um comício com apoiadores venezuelanos durante sua visita à Espanha — Foto: REUTERS/Isabel Infantes

A líder da oposição venezuelana, Maria Corina Machado, retornou à Venezuela neste domingo (25) após passar quase um ano fora do país.

A volta foi confirmada por Machado em suas redes sociais e também pelo ex-candidato presidencial Edmundo González —que concorreu contra o ditador Nicolás Maduro em 2024.

"Estou aqui. Com vocês", afirmou Machado em sua conta no X. "Venezuela! Estou muito feliz em anunciar que nossa líder, minha querida Maria Corina, está em território venezuelano", escreveu González.

O retorno de Corina Machado ocorre após diversas tentativas frustradas de voltar à Venezuela nas últimas semanas.

Corina Machado havia deixado a Venezuela em dezembro após ter vencido o prêmio Nobel da Paz e ter passado meses escondida em meio à repressão do governo Maduro. Sua saída do país, inclusive, foi possibilitada por uma operação secreta chefiada pelo governo Trump.

Ainda não se sabe qual será a atuação dela no cenário político da Venezuela neste retorno. O governo da presidente interina Delcy Rodriguez, que sucedeu Maduro após operação militar dos EUA que o depôs, é acusado de ser uma continuidade do chavismo.

articles.summary: Eleições de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos, agendadas para 3 de novembro, renovarão toda a Câmara dos Deputados e um terço do Senado. Donald Trump tenta preservar o controle de seu partido sobre o Congresso do país.
articles.body:
Presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, conversa com jornalistas após votar antecipadamente nas midterms na Flórida, nos Estados Unidos, em 25 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Umit Bektas

O presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , votou no sábado (24) de forma antecipada nas eleições de meio de mandato , as midterms, após críticas à modalidade de votação.

Trump estava acompanhado da primeira-dama Melania Trump quando compareceu a um local de votação em West Palm Beach, na Flórida, para dar seu voto.

O líder norte-americano falou com a imprensa após votar. Perguntado se teria votado a favor de seu partido, o Republicano, Trump disse que "com toda a certeza".

Trump também falou sobre outros assuntos, como as guerras da Ucrânia e do Irã. Ele elogiou as habilidades de negociação de Melania, que segundo a Casa Branca foi responsável por um cessar-fogo localizado entre a Rússia e a Ucrânia na cidade de Oleshky, controlada pelos russos.

O presidente norte-americano também disse que cabe ao Irã decidir, ao ser questionado sobre possíveis novos ataques dos Estados Unidos contra o país.

“E a questão é: terminamos o trabalho, o que não seria muito difícil? Ou fazemos um acordo com eles?”, disse Trump, acrescentando: “E isso vai depender deles”.

As eleições de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos, agendadas para 3 de novembro, renovarão toda a Câmara dos Deputados e um terço do Senado. Donald Trump tenta preservar o controle de seu partido sobre o Congresso do país. Leia mais sobre as midterms.

O candidato ao governo do Rio Grande do Norte Cadu de Lula (PT) votou na manhã deste domingo (25), no Colégio Marista, em Natal . Ele estava acompanhado de familiares e aliados políticos .

Após votar, o candidato avaliou a campanha do primeiro e do segundo turno e disse estar confiante no resultado das urnas.

articles.title: El Salvador president says bodies found in Haiti do not belong to ambushed soldiers
articles.summary: SAN SALVADOR/PORT-AU-PRINCE, Oct 24 (Reuters) - Four bodies handed over to Salvadoran forces on Saturday do not belong to the four soldiers who had been ambu...
articles.body:
SAN SALVADOR/PORT-AU-PRINCE, Oct 24 (Reuters) - Four bodies handed over to Salvadoran forces on Saturday do not belong to the four soldiers who had been ‌ambushed the previous Sunday outside the capital of Haiti, El Salvador President ‌Nayib Bukele said, contradicting a New York Times report.

"They are not our men," Bukele said in a ​post on X, hours after The New York Times reported that the bodies had been found and were believed to be those of the Salvadoran soldiers.

The four went missing on Sunday after they jumped from a burning armored vehicle that came under attack on ‌the outskirts of Port-au-Prince while ⁠they were returning from a market to their base.

Bukele said the four bodies handed over included a child, a man much taller ⁠than the Salvadorans and a soldier from another country. He shared photos of a soldier's identification from Chad.

The ambush was the first major attack on the Gang Suppression Force, a ​UN-authorized ​multinational mission, since it began operations in Haiti ​this year. The international security mission ‌declined to comment on the matter.

Earlier this week, Bukele said gangs were holding the four men and that El Salvador had launched a military operation to bring them back unharmed. Additional Salvadoran troops were later deployed to support search and security operations.

No group has publicly claimed responsibility for the attack. Local media have linked the ambush to ‌gangs operating in the area, including powerful armed ​groups Chen Mechan and 400 Mawozo.

A year into ​its mandate, the GSF has about ​2,000 troops on the ground, well below its authorized ceiling ‌of 5,500. An earlier Kenyan-led security effort ​struggled with chronic shortages ​of money, equipment and personnel.

Haiti's gangs have expanded sharply since the 2021 assassination of President Jovenel Moise, taking control of large parts of Port-au-Prince and ​displacing 1.4 million to 1.5 ‌million people.

(Reporting by Kylie Madry in Mexico City, Harold Isaac in Port-au-Prince ​and Gerardo Arbaiza in San Salvador; Writing by Sarah Morland; Editing by ​Alistair Bell, Rod Nickel and David Gregorio)

articles.title: A 24-year-old US Coast Guard swimmer spent two hours in darkness and 6-to-8-foot waves rescuing 16 people from the Pacific off Mexico; 11 others remain missing after the October 16 boat disaster
articles.summary: A heroic 24-year-old US Coast Guard swimmer, Josh Law, rescued 16 people from a capsized boat in the rough Pacific waters off Mexico, while 11 others remain missing. The intense operation faced 6-to-8-foot waves and total darkness.
articles.body: A 24-year-old US Coast Guard rescue swimmer spent two hours battling rough seas in near-total darkness to save 16 people after a boat capsized in the Pacific Ocean off Mexico’s Baja California peninsula. Eleven others remain missing after an extensive search was called off.Josh Law was lowered from a Coast Guard helicopter into the ocean during the early hours of October 16, with waves reaching 6 to 8 feet (1.8 to 2.4 metres). Guided by a searchlight from the aircraft, he searched the water for survivors scattered across the area.“I was experiencing exhaustion at that point,” Law told The Associated Press in his first interview since the operation. “We had very little sleep. But what I was experiencing was nothing compared to what they were at that point ... I just had to keep that in mind.”The rescue unfolded about 140 miles (225 kilometres) off Mexico’s coast. Law was the only rescuer in the water during the operation, pulling survivors towards a basket lowered from the helicopter. The crew hoisted each person aboard before lowering the basket again.The Coast Guard suspended its search for the remaining 11 people late on Sunday after teams from the United States and Mexico, alongside the US Navy, searched more than 2,441 square miles (6,322 square kilometres) over a combined 89 hours.Mayday call triggers overnight rescueThe emergency began at around 1 am, when a distress call reported that a boat was sinking in the Pacific off Ensenada, Mexico. Within minutes, an alarm woke Law and other crew members at US Coast Guard Air Station Ventura, northwest of Los Angeles.Helicopter pilot Lieutenant Miyako Miller checked the flying conditions and planned a route over the ocean. Law prepared his dry suit, fins and medical supplies before securing himself in a harness designed to lower him from the aircraft.The crew took off from Ventura at about 2am. Miller used night-vision goggles to navigate without moonlight, relying on the stars to maintain her bearings.As the helicopter neared the reported location, she spotted a faint light in the distance. The crew then saw what appeared to be debris floating on the surface, although the darkness made it difficult to identify.Miller manoeuvred the aircraft until it hovered about 40 feet (12 metres) above the water while the flight mechanic guided her positioning.“I’m doing my best to maintain my references externally by looking outside through the night vision goggles,” Miller said, describing how she relied on visual cues while the mechanic directed the helicopter.Swimmer pulled survivors from rough seasLaw entered the water as the helicopter’s rotor blades churned up spray and turbulence. The noise made it difficult to hear, while the darkness limited what he could see beyond the crew’s searchlight.The people in the water were spread across a wide area. Some wore life jackets with small lights, while others held on to one another, buoys or pieces of wreckage as they tried to stay afloat.Law said he swam towards each survivor, turned them onto their backs and used a rescue method known as a “buddy tow”, placing an arm over the person while kicking towards the helicopter’s pickup point.“With one hand, I’m holding the survivor. With the other, I am signalling to the helicopter and working with the device,” he said.At the designated point, Law signalled for the flight mechanic to lower a rescue basket. He placed each survivor inside before the crew raised the basket into the aircraft. The process was repeated until 16 people had been rescued.As the operation continued, water gradually filled Law’s dry suit to his knees, adding weight as he repeatedly swam through the waves.The helicopter crew faced a separate constraint as fuel supplies dwindled and the aircraft filled with survivors. They decided to fly to a Coast Guard station in San Diego, where ambulances were waiting.During the flight, Law treated three people with serious wounds and worked to stop their bleeding. The Coast Guard said some injuries were consistent with shark bites and that its personnel provided emergency first aid.Investigation continues into cause of disasterThe rescued people were all Mexican nationals, according to the Mexican consulate. The circumstances surrounding the boat’s voyage remain under investigation, including where it departed from and why it was so far offshore.The Coast Guard said US Customs and Border Protection was investigating the incident and interviewing survivors. The agency did not respond to multiple requests for information on whether the boat was involved in migrant smuggling.Officials have not established whether the vessel became lost, suffered engine failure, was swept out to sea or was intended to travel that distance. Only pieces of the boat were recovered.After the survivors received medical treatment, Customs and Border Protection officers said they would be processed under US immigration law. US officials said nearly half of those rescued had since been returned to Mexico.Law and the rest of the crew returned to Ventura on the morning of October 16. He described it as the longest rescue operation he had undertaken.The search for the missing people continued for another two days before being suspended without finding the remaining 11.The incident occurred along a remote stretch of the Pacific used by boats travelling from Mexico’s Baja California peninsula. Migrants increasingly turn to dangerous sea routes offered by smugglers to avoid heavily guarded land borders. articles.title: BSF apprehends four Pakistani fishermen in Kutch, seizes boat
articles.summary: The Border Security Force (BSF) has apprehended four Pakistani fishermen who allegedly entered Indian waters for crab-catching activities and seized a
articles.body: The Border Security Force (BSF) has apprehended four Pakistani fishermen who allegedly entered Indian waters for crab-catching activities and seized a fishing boat near the India-Pakistan border in Gujarat’s Kutch district.According to news agency PTI, the fishermen were apprehended from the Sir Creek area on Sunday following specific intelligence inputs, an official said. The fishermen were identified as Kadir Thaimor, Muhammad Mussa, Azgar Thaimor and Ahsan Jat, all residents of Chach Jaan Khan village in Pakistan’s Sindh province, according to information provided by the BSF.Sir Creek is a narrow, marshy tidal channel in the Rann of Kutch, along the coastal region between Gujarat and Pakistan’s Sindh province. The area is strategically sensitive because the longstanding India-Pakistan boundary dispute over the creek affects the demarcation of the maritime boundary in the Arabian Sea.The region’s shallow waters, tidal channels and extensive marshlands make navigation and border surveillance challenging. Fishing activities in the area can also lead to fishermen crossing into the other country’s waters, prompting apprehensions by security personnel.The BSF maintains surveillance along the sensitive western border to prevent unauthorised crossings and other illegal activities. The latest apprehension follows an operation based on specific intelligence inputs, during which the four fishermen and their boat were taken into custody.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Jessie James Decker shares 'secret sauce' behind family's food, faith, traditions
articles.summary: Country singer Jessie James Decker reveals her family's game day food traditions, favorite recipes and how Catholic faith shapes life around the dinner table.
articles.body: Country singer Jessie James Decker has spent years balancing music and business with raising a growing family, but some of her favorite moments happen around the dinner table. Decker recently released "The Secret Sauce: A Family Cookbook Seasoned with Love," which she wrote with her mother, Karen Parker, and sister Sydney Rae Bass. The cookbook draws on the family's Southern, Sicilian and Cajun roots, bringing together recipes and traditions passed down through generations and shared at family gatherings. It includes everything from weeknight meals and game-day dishes to holiday recipes and desserts. CELEBRITY CHEF SAYS PEOPLE HAVE SOUTHERN FOOD ALL WRONG, SHARES WHAT HER FAMILY ATE For Jessie James Decker, food is closely connected to both family and faith. The singer and author told Fox News Digital that her Catholic faith has long played an important role in her family, something she credits her mother with passing down. "Faith has always been a big part of my life and our lives," Jessie James Decker said. She said her mother taught the family to turn to prayer during both difficult and joyful seasons of life. CELEBRITY CHEF SAYS MILITARY LESSON IS KEY TO KEEPING FAMILIES TOGETHER "You just have to trust in Him, because His plan is so much greater than you could ever imagine," Jessie James Decker said. Those values also carry into life at home with her husband, former NFL wide receiver Eric Decker, and their four children. One of the family's traditions is sitting down together for dinner, with electronics put away, so everyone has a chance to catch up. "It's not even that hard to get rid of the electronics when it's time for dinner because we want to talk to each other," Jessie James Decker said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "We just get so excited to have that time with each other, to be present, to ask about each other's day." Jessie James Decker said she often goes around the table and asks each child a question, sometimes something silly, to get everyone talking. "Those memories and moments with my family around the dinner table are just my favorite," she said. Cooking itself has become another way Jessie James Decker connects with her children. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES She described making food as one of her strongest "love languages," saying she takes pride in preparing meals for her family and watching her children enjoy them. "I just get such pride, such joy from making food to nourish their bodies and fill their tummies," Jessie James Decker said. "The secret sauce is just the love and joy that you put into cooking." Her children have already developed their own favorites from her kitchen. Daughter Vivi loves seafood gumbo, while sons Eric and Forrest enjoy her pasta dishes. Her youngest, Denver, is also a gumbo fan, Jessie James Decker said. Her husband's football background has also shaped some of their food traditions. On game days, Jessie James Decker said she typically makes chili, barbecue meatballs and some type of dip, occasionally adding wings to the spread. "Every game day we definitely get after it," she said. articles.title: Fugitive mom wanted in daughter’s Arizona murder used cartels to hide for years before capture in Mexico: feds
articles.summary: Anna Marlene Somoza's cartel connections helped her evade U.S. Marshals for over 12 years as a fugitive in Mexico after her daughter's 1997 death.
articles.body: Nearly 30 years after the death of her 3-year-old daughter, a mother has been arrested in Mexico by U.S. law enforcement officers on first-degree murder charges. Anna Marlene Somoza, 60, was arrested by the U.S. Marshals Service after more than 12 years as a fugitive in Mexico. Her close connections to cartels allowed her to avoid apprehension, authorities said. Somoza will be extradited to the United States to face charges for allegedly murdering her daughter, Crystal Reyes, according to the U.S. Marshals Service. MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING PARTNER ARRESTED IN MEXICO NEARLY TWO YEARS AFTER FLEEING WITH THEIR TWO CHILDREN Before her death, Reyes was subjected to severe abuse, torture and starvation, the agency said. Confined to a small dog kennel, Reyes was bound by her hands and feet, gagged and left for weeks at a time. On Jan. 30, 1997, Reyes was bound, suffocated with a towel taped to her face, and left to die inside a sealed cardboard box, the agency said. DNA TECHNOLOGY LEADS TO ARREST IN 1988 KILLING OF ORLANDO WOMAN AFTER NEARLY FOUR DECADES Authorities began investigating after human bone fragments were found in a deserted area of Arizona by a hunter in November 1998. Almost two decades passed. Then in August 2014, forensic DNA analysis identified the fragments of bone as remains of Reyes. FORENSIC GENEALOGY UNMASKS COLD CASE SUSPECT AS STRANGLER, SEXUAL PREDATOR DECADES LATER: OFFICIALS Detectives interviewed the child’s biological father and confirmed her identity using his DNA. Then, they said, they had sufficient grounds to charge Somoza and Avelino Tamala, her boyfriend at the time of Reyes’ death, with first-degree murder in December 2014. Tamala was found guilty of Crystal’s murder in 2016. He was sentenced to life in prison. DRUG CARTEL KINGPIN AMONG TARGETS IN SWEEPING TRUMP CRACKDOWN ON ALLEGED MEXICAN CORRUPTION NETWORK But Somoza had been deported years earlier. Criminal past Somoza had an extensive criminal history before being charged in her daughter’s death. She had been connected to a major transnational drug trafficking network active along the southern Arizona border throughout the 1980s and 1990s. After her 1993 arrest for the sale and transportation of marijuana, she agreed to act as a confidential informant for an Arizona law enforcement agency. Through that, she met Tamala, a narcotics detective, and began "an improper romantic relationship," according to the U.S. Marshals Service. SAN JOSE GIRL, 8, DIES AFTER LIVING IN COCKROACH-INFESTED HOME AS MOTHER, STEPFATHER FACE CHARGES Not long after Reyes’ birth in Mexico in 1993, the mother and daughter began living with Tamala in Arizona, according to the agency. Tamala was not the father of Reyes. The abuse Reyes endured likely wasn’t caught because she wasn’t attending school, said Stacy Vaughan, vice president of growth and prevention at Childhelp, a child abuse prevention organization. "The majority of reports come from the education system in our country, from teachers, counselors, schools," Vaughan told Fox News Digital. But a case like this may be prevented with the modern legislation in the United States, she said. "In the past 20 years, many states have passed laws not only mandating that professionals report any suspected abuse, but…every adult over the age of 18 is considered a mandated reporter." Cold case In 1999, the year after Reyes’ remains were found, Somoza and Tamala were arrested on drug- and weapon-related charges. Somoza served eight years in federal prison and was deported in 2008. After the child’s remains were connected to her as the mother in 2014, investigators from five state and federal agencies began to search for her. articles.title: Israel elections: Can Benjamin Netanyahu turn security gains into a political victory?
articles.summary: Three years after the October 7 attack, Benjamin Netanyahu faces a crucial electoral test over security, political accountability and the direction of
articles.body: Three years after the October 7 attack, Benjamin Netanyahu faces a crucial electoral test over security, political accountability and the direction of Israel.Donald Trump’s endorsement and the unresolved confrontation with Iran have raised the stakes, but a divided opposition may struggle to turn its challenge into power.Israelis vote on Tuesday, October 27, in the country's first general election since Hamas's October 7, 2023, terrorist attack. The outcome could determine whether Bibi, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, extends his political career or loses power after three years of war and domestic turmoil.The final opinion polls suggest a close contest. Surveys published by Israel's three major television networks on Friday put Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party ahead of Netanyahu's Likud. Yet neither the prime minister's coalition nor the main opposition bloc is projected to secure the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member Knesset.Yashar was projected to win around 22-23 seats, against 19-21 for Likud. Netanyahu's coalition was projected at about 50 seats, while the main opposition bloc was estimated at 52-56. Arab-led parties could win another 14-16 seats.These are projections, not results. But they point to the central question of the election: can Netanyahu survive the verdict on his leadership and can his opponents agree on an alternative?The challenger: Gadi EisenkotEisenkot, a former chief of the Israel Defence Forces (IDF), has emerged as Netanyahu's principal challenger. He served as military chief from 2015 to 2019 and joined the wartime government formed after the October 7 attack.He left the government in June 2024, arguing that political considerations were influencing decisions on the war. He subsequently broke with Benny Gantz and established Yashar in September 2025.Eisenkot's appeal rests on military experience, greater accountability and the argument that Israel needs a change of leadership without abandoning its security priorities.He is not a conventional left-wing challenger. His criticism centres on Netanyahu's handling of the war, the failures that preceded October 7 and the government's domestic agenda. Like several other opposition figures, he takes a hard line on Hamas and argues that Israel needs more effective security leadership.This distinction matters. The election is not a straightforward contest between hawkish and dovish approaches. Many of Netanyahu's opponents argue that his decisions have weakened Israel's security rather than strengthened it.October 7 and accountabilityThe October 7 attack remains the defining test of Netanyahu's leadership.Hamas-led militants killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel and took 251 hostages, according to Israeli figures. The attack exposed major failures in intelligence, military preparedness and the government's assessment of Hamas's intentions.Netanyahu has emphasised the military campaigns that followed, presenting his government as determined to dismantle Hamas and confront threats from Iran and its regional allies. His critics argue that the attack happened under his watch and that the government has yet to provide an adequate account of how Israel's security establishment failed to prevent it.Opposition parties and critics have demanded an independent state commission of inquiry. Netanyahu has resisted such an investigation, which could scrutinise decisions taken by his government as well as the military and intelligence services.In recent weeks, reports said he had advance warning from the UAE and Egypt that Hamas was planning an attack. He calls the claims libellous and is taking legal action against the outlets that published them.His personal legal troubles add another layer. Netanyahu is on trial on charges of bribery, fraud and breach of trust, which he denies. In November 2025, he asked President Isaac Herzog for a pardon without admitting guilt, following public pressure from Trump. The trial remains a separate legal process.He is also subject to an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over alleged war crimes in Gaza, which he rejects.For his supporters, Netanyahu remains an experienced leader facing extraordinary security challenges. For his opponents, his political survival has become inseparable from questions of accountability.Dr Ashok Sharma, a visiting fellow at the University of New South Wales in Canberra, said the October 7 attacks had damaged Netanyahu's reputation as Israel's most experienced security-oriented leader. However, he cautioned against underestimating the prime minister's political resilience.“His supporters increasingly assess his leadership through Israel’s subsequent military campaigns against Hamas, Hezbollah and Iran,” Sharma said, adding that these operations had demonstrated Israel's military capabilities and determination to confront regional threats.For conservative and nationalist voters, he said, security remains a priority. The election will test whether accountability for October 7 outweighs confidence in Netanyahu's ability to confront continuing threats.Iran war: Security asset or political liability?Security is Netanyahu's central campaign argument and Iran is where it has become most consequential.Israel and the United States launched military operations against Iran on February 28, targeting its nuclear and military infrastructure.The conflict widened into a regional confrontation before a Pakistan-mediated process produced a ceasefire arrangement and a memorandum of understanding in June.The pause has not resolved the underlying disputes. Iran's nuclear programme, sanctions and the Strait of Hormuz remain sources of tension, while pressure on Iranian ports and continuing regional uncertainty have kept the risk of renewed fighting alive.Netanyahu has presented the campaign against Iran as a strategic achievement, arguing that military action has weakened a major threat to Israel. He maintains that further action may be necessary to prevent Tehran from rebuilding its capabilities or pursuing a nuclear weapon.But the war also raises questions about its costs, its long-term results and whether military operations have delivered a sustainable outcome.Sharma said the campaign had demonstrated Israel's intelligence capabilities, technological superiority and ability to project military power. However, he cautioned that Iran retained the capacity for asymmetric retaliation and could rebuild its military capabilities.“Military achievements alone cannot guarantee lasting security,” he said, arguing that the campaign's ultimate success would depend on whether military gains could be translated into sustainable deterrence, diplomatic arrangements and regional stability.The conflict has also highlighted Israel's dependence on American military assistance, intelligence cooperation and diplomatic support. Sharma described this as a strategic partnership rather than simply a vulnerability, while noting that the long-term outcome would depend on how effectively Israel converts its military gains into lasting security.A Financial Times report published earlier this week added a new dimension to the election.Citing people familiar with the plans, it reported that Netanyahu had instructed the Israeli military to prepare a major offensive against Iran for the weekend of October 10. The newspaper said Trump opposed restarting the fighting before the November 3 US midterm elections. Netanyahu subsequently rejected the account as incorrect and biased.The episode highlights a central question for Israeli voters: how much freedom does Netanyahu have to pursue his preferred military strategy without American backing?The US is Israel's most consequential international partner, providing military assistance and diplomatic support. Even when the two governments agree on the threat posed by Iran, they may differ over the timing and consequences of further attacks.For Netanyahu, the Iran campaign supports his longstanding argument that Israel needs a leader prepared to take decisive action. His opponents can counter that successive rounds of military escalation and ceasefires do not amount to a durable security strategy.A change of government would not necessarily bring a major shift in policy. Eisenkot and other opposition figures have also taken a hard line on Iran and have mostly attacked Netanyahu from the right, calling him soft on security.Hence, the difference may lie less in whether Israel regards Tehran as a threat than in how a new government chooses to manage it.Trump backs Netanyahu — but the relationship has limitsTrump has made his preference clear. On October 18, he publicly endorsed Netanyahu's re-election, praising him as a strong leader and arguing that another prime minister might leave Washington to confront Iran alone.Netanyahu has used the endorsement to reinforce his claim that his personal relationship with Trump helps protect Israeli interests.Sharma said the endorsement strengthened Netanyahu's image as an internationally experienced leader capable of maintaining Washington's support. He pointed to the wider record of US-Israel cooperation, including American recognition of Jerusalem as Israel's capital and Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights, as well as the Abraham Accords.But the relationship is not unconditional. The reported disagreement over a possible renewed offensive against Iran suggests that Washington's calculations, including the US domestic political calendar, may not always align with Netanyahu's military priorities.Netanyahu has disputed the reporting, but the broader tension remains relevant.Trump's endorsement also allows Netanyahu to present the election as a choice between continuity in Israel's relationship with Washington and a potentially less predictable alternative.Yet American support cannot by itself resolve his domestic difficulties or guarantee a parliamentary majority. Sharma said the endorsement could consolidate Netanyahu's support among conservative and security-conscious voters, but Israeli elections would still be shaped by domestic security, economic conditions and coalition politics.Netanyahu has also used his campaign to portray his opponents as aligned with forces hostile to Israel. In August, he shared an image of a Likud campaign billboard featuring New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani alongside Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem. The message suggested that these figures wanted Netanyahu to lose and urged voters not to let them win.Mamdani, a vocal critic of Israel's conduct in Gaza, has called Netanyahu a war criminal and urged the US government to enforce the International Criminal Court's arrest warrant if he travelled to New York.Also read: 'Don't let them win' - Netanyahu's party puts Zohran Mamdani alongside Iran, Hezbollah leaders on billboardThe billboard illustrated Netanyahu's attempt to frame the election as more than a domestic contest over governance. For his supporters, it reinforced the argument that Israel needs a leader prepared to confront its adversaries. Critics may see it as an effort to shift attention away from accountability and domestic problems.The US relationship itself has become more politically contested, particularly over the war in Gaza. Even if Netanyahu remains in office, he will have to manage American political divisions alongside the strategic partnership.Domestic fault linesNetanyahu's political strength has long depended on alliances among right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties. These partnerships have enabled him to govern but have also constrained his room for manoeuvre.One of the sharpest disputes concerns military service. Ultra-Orthodox parties have defended exemptions for many men engaged in full-time religious study. As prolonged military operations have increased the demands on reservists and their families, the exemptions have become a more contentious political issue.Israel's Supreme Court ruled in 2024 that the broad legal basis for the exemptions could not continue as it had. Critics argue that the burden of defending the country should be shared more fairly, while ultra-Orthodox parties regard protecting religious study as a core commitment.Eisenkot has made broader military service one of his priorities, putting him at odds with parties that want to preserve the exemptions.The election also reopens the dispute over judicial reform. Netanyahu's government pursued controversial changes to the judicial system in 2023, prompting mass protests and warnings that the proposals would weaken checks on executive power. The war interrupted that confrontation but did not settle it.These disputes could complicate coalition negotiations even if Netanyahu's Likud performs strongly. They also give the opposition an opportunity to argue that a change of leadership could address domestic divisions without abandoning Israel's security priorities.Arithmetic problemIsrael's parliamentary system means that winning the most seats does not automatically make a party's leader prime minister. The president consults political factions after the election before asking a candidate to form a government.That candidate normally has 28 days to assemble a coalition, with a possible 14-day extension. The key requirement is support from at least 61 of the Knesset's 120 members.This is where the opposition faces its biggest obstacle. Its parties may collectively win more seats than Netanyahu's coalition, but they disagree over which partners they are willing to accept.Arab-led parties could prove pivotal, with final polls projecting them at 14-16 seats combined. But Eisenkot and other opposition figures have faced pressure over whether they would rely on their support to form a government.That leaves several possibilities: an opposition-led government relying on Arab parties from outside the coalition, unexpected alliances or defections from Netanyahu-aligned parties. A national unity government is another possibility, although the failed 2020 power-sharing arrangement between Netanyahu and Benny Gantz offers little assurance of stability.Netanyahu has portrayed cooperation between his opponents and Arab parties as a threat, arguing that the election is a choice between the political right and a government that would concede too much to Palestinian interests.His opponents say the priority should be accountability and effective governance, but their divisions make it difficult to present a clear alternative.Sharma said the opposition's ideological differences could prove a major obstacle even if it secures enough seats collectively to challenge Netanyahu. Disagreements over national security, judicial reform, religious issues and relations with the Palestinians could also undermine the stability of any coalition it manages to form.Netanyahu, meanwhile, has extensive experience in coalition negotiations and has repeatedly demonstrated political resilience. Sharma said another fragmented Knesset, prolonged negotiations or political deadlock remained realistic possibilities.Netanyahu could therefore survive even if his coalition falls short of a majority, simply because his opponents cannot agree on a replacement.What happens next?The final polls are not guarantees. Netanyahu has beaten unfavourable surveys before, including in 2015, when the final polling picture underestimated his eventual performance. Smaller parties could also alter the balance if they unexpectedly cross or fail to cross the 3.25% threshold required to enter the Knesset.If no candidate can assemble a viable majority, Israel could face another election. Netanyahu would remain caretaker prime minister in the interim, leaving the country with many of the same unresolved questions.The consequences would extend beyond domestic politics. Israel's next government will have to manage the confrontation with Iran, maintain its relationship with Washington, address the aftermath of the Gaza war and respond to questions about the security failures that preceded October 7.Those challenges will remain regardless of who wins.An opposition victory, however, would not necessarily mean a fundamental change in Israel's security and foreign policy. Sharma said countering Iran's nuclear ambitions and regional influence, maintaining military superiority and preserving the US-Israel strategic partnership would remain central priorities under any government.He also expects Israel's strategic relationship with India to remain largely unaffected by a change of leadership, given the established cooperation in defence technology, cybersecurity, intelligence and emerging technologies. An opposition government could place greater emphasis on diplomatic coordination with Washington, European partners and regional states, but the broader strategic direction would likely remain intact.“An opposition victory would therefore be more likely to change Israel’s diplomatic style and regional engagement than fundamentally alter its strategic orientation,” Sharma said.For Netanyahu, Tuesday's vote is a test of whether his security-first strategy can survive the failures of October 7 and the consequences of the wars that followed. For Eisenkot and the opposition, the challenge is to convert dissatisfaction with the prime minister into a stable governing majority.Trump's endorsement and the Iran confrontation have given Netanyahu a powerful argument for continuity. But they have also exposed the limits of his control: Israeli military decisions remain tied to American calculations, while the costs of prolonged conflict continue to shape domestic politics.Netanyahu's future is on the ballot. Whether Israel's political direction changes with it will depend not only on the votes cast but on who can assemble the 61 seats needed to govern.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: ‘A defeat for the Republic’: How October 17 protest fiasco shaped France’s security strategy
articles.summary: France deployed 70,000 security personnel across the country on October 24, backed by elite police units, helicopters, drones and armoured vehicles, as
articles.body: France deployed 70,000 security personnel across the country on October 24, backed by elite police units, helicopters, drones and armoured vehicles, as authorities sought to prevent a repeat of the violence that engulfed several cities a week earlier. The show of force followed widespread criticism of the government’s handling of nationwide demonstrations over education funding, rising living costs and deteriorating public services.The October 17 protests exposed serious shortcomings in France’s ability to anticipate and contain unrest, with rioters attacking shops, public buildings and police vehicles. In Limoges, a fire severely damaged the historic town hall, while other cities witnessed arson, looting and clashes with security forces. Interior minister Laurent Nuñez acknowledged that police had lost control in some areas, prompting President Emmanuel Macron to demand answers over the intelligence and planning failures.An investigation by French outlet Mediapart, published on October 24, described an administration struggling to comprehend the scale of the unrest and scrambling to prepare for the next mobilisation. The failures behind October 17The October 17 demonstrations grew out of student protests that began in September over overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages, deteriorating school infrastructure and inadequate funding. The movement subsequently attracted trade unions, parents, farmers and other groups frustrated by rising fuel prices, living costs and pressure on public services.The interior ministry estimated that 550,000 people participated in the October 17 mobilisation, while the CGT trade union put the figure above 800,000. Although most demonstrations were peaceful, violence spread across multiple cities, overwhelming police resources and exposing gaps in operational planning.According to Mediapart, senior officials privately described the episode as an unprecedented failure. One senior administrative official called it “a defeat for the Republic”, while another told the outlet that authorities had been “completely overwhelmed”.The investigation identified inadequate police deployment relative to the scale of the unrest as a central problem. Officers struggled to protect multiple locations as groups of rioters moved beyond the main demonstrations, targeting commercial districts and public buildings.The scale of the violence also challenged established policing assumptions. One official cited by Mediapart questioned how authorities could have anticipated thousands of people confronting police in Limoges. The report portrayed intelligence failures as part of the explanation, but suggested that the authorities’ difficulties extended beyond intelligence gathering to the broader challenge of managing simultaneous outbreaks of violence.Macron publicly demanded answers, saying he had instructed the government to ensure such a breakdown did not happen again. Nuñez, who had offered his resignation, remained in office, but faced mounting pressure to demonstrate that the state could restore control. 70,000 officers and a message of ‘utmost firmness’The government’s response was markedly different ahead of October 24. In a telegram sent to prefects on October 22, which Mediapart reviewed, Nuñez instructed officials to implement the security measures with “the utmost firmness”.SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'You use AI every day. articles.title: A Wisconsin dairy farmer sprained his ankle and began sculpting; 15 years later, Nick Engelbert had transformed his farmhouse into Grandview, with over 40 statues and colourful decorations
articles.summary: A sprained ankle changed the course of Nick Engelbert’s life on his small farm in Hollandale, Wisconsin.
articles.body: A sprained ankle changed the course of Nick Engelbert’s life on his small farm in Hollandale, Wisconsin. An Austrian immigrant who made his living as a dairy farmer, Engelbert began working with concrete and found objects, eventually turning his farmhouse and yard into an unusual collection of handmade art. Broken china, pieces of glass, buttons, beads and seashells became part of the surfaces he decorated, while the grounds gradually filled with figures drawn from American politics, folklore, history and his own imagination. What began with a single sculpture grew over the next 15 years into a display of more than 40 works, giving the property its own distinctive character.How a sprained ankle inspired Nick Engelbert’s folk artNick Engelbert was born in Austria in 1881 and later settled in Wisconsin, where he worked as a dairy farmer. His home in Hollandale became known as Grandview, a name that reflected the broad views across the surrounding countryside. For years, the property served as his home and workplace, but a visit to the Dickeyville Grotto around 1930 introduced him to a different way of using concrete.The grotto, an elaborate assemblage of religious and decorative structures made with cement and colourful objects, appears to have left a lasting impression on Engelbert. He began adapting some of those ideas at home, although his own work would draw on a much wider range of subjects. A sprained ankle is associated with the beginning of his sculptural work, giving him a reason to turn his attention towards a project that did not depend on his usual farm duties.Engelbert started with concrete, gradually learning how to shape and decorate it. The work spread beyond a single object. His farmhouse became part of the undertaking, with the exterior covered in concrete and embedded fragments of china, glass, beads, buttons and shells. An arched porch framed the entrance, giving the building an appearance unlike that of a conventional rural home.Nick Engelbert created more than 40 concrete sculptures to transform Grandview’s groundsThe changes to Grandview did not stop at the walls. Over roughly 15 years, Engelbert created more than 40 sculptures for the surrounding grounds, making use of the space around his house as an outdoor display. Some pieces drew on familiar symbols, while others reflected stories, historical figures and scenes that he devised himself.Eagles and castles featured among the works, alongside planters, a Viking aboard a ship and an organ grinder. Their subjects were varied, and the collection did not follow a single theme. Engelbert moved between patriotic imagery, fairy tales and mythology, using the same basic material to produce objects with different forms and meanings.The decorations also made use of materials that might otherwise have been discarded. Small pieces of glass and china, along with buttons and beads, were pressed into the concrete to add colour and detail. Rather than relying on paint alone, Engelbert built the decoration into the surfaces themselves. The result was a house and garden that shared a common visual style.A sculpture that brought politics into the gardenAmong Engelbert’s more pointed creations was a work titled How do you expect to get a day’s work out of a team like this. It depicted Uncle Sam attempting to plough with a donkey and an elephant, the animals associated with the Democratic and Republican parties in American politics.The joke depended on the contrast between the familiar image of a farmer working a team in a field and the political symbolism of the animals pulling the plough. It also reflected Engelbert’s interest in subjects beyond farm life. His sculptures could draw on national identity and public affairs just as readily as they could on legends or imagined characters.The political piece sat alongside works with no obvious connection to current events. A castle, a Viking ship and an organ grinder belonged to different worlds, yet all became part of the same garden. Engelbert’s approach allowed these subjects to coexist without the collection needing to tell one continuous story.At 70, Nick Engelbert turned from concrete sculptures to paintingBy the time Engelbert reached 70, he could no longer continue making sculptures. He turned instead to painting, producing more than 200 oil paintings during the final period of his life. The change brought a different working method, but it allowed him to keep making art after the physical demands of building large concrete figures had become harder to manage.Engelbert died in 1962, aged 80 or 81, depending on how his age is calculated from his birth year. His work at Grandview had developed over decades, beginning with changes to the farmhouse and expanding into a collection of sculptures that reflected his interests and imagination.Grandview’s legacy as a Wisconsin folk art landmarkEngelbert’s property is remembered as an example of folk art created outside formal artistic institutions. He was a farmer rather than a trained sculptor, and his work developed through practical experimentation with concrete and decorative materials. The house itself became part of the display, while the sculptures brought together political humour, familiar stories and subjects from his imagination.The collection’s origins lay in a modest change of routine, but its scale grew through years of work. Engelbert transformed the setting around his home without abandoning the rural character of the property. His sculptures were not separate from everyday life on the farm; they occupied the same land where he had lived and worked.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
