articles.title: Worse winter pollution looms as Kol breaches PM10 limit
articles.summary: Kolkata breaches India’s annual PM10 limit by mid-October, averaging 76 µg/m³ in 2026 (up 5.6%), raising concerns of worse winter air pollution.
articles.body: Kolkata: Winter is yet to set in, but Kolkata has already exceeded its annual PM10 pollution level. An analysis of air-quality monitoring data by CREA (Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air) has revealed that the city accumulated enough particulate pollution by mid-Oct to breach India’s annual air-quality benchmark — 60 µg/m³ — even if its air were to remain completely free of PM10 for the rest of the year.This has led to fears of a more polluted winter.The findings suggest that Kolkata is entering its most pollution-prone months with an already excessive burden of airborne particles, raising fresh concerns over the city’s deteriorating air quality.According to an analysis by CREA’s lead researcher Manoj Kumar, based on Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) continuous monitoring data, Kolkata’s average PM10 concentration between Jan 1 and Oct 16 stood at 76 micrograms per cubic metre (µg/m³), up from 72 µg/m³ during the corresponding period in 2025. This represents an increase of nearly 6%, reversing the improvement observed over previous years.India’s National Ambient Air Quality Standards prescribe an annual PM10 limit of 60 µg/m³. The World Health Organization’s recommended annual guideline is considerably stricter, just 15 µg/m³. Kolkata’s average concentration during the study period was therefore more than five times the WHO guideline.The CREA researchers adopted an unusual approach to illustrate the accumulated pollution burden. They calculated the cumulative PM10 concentration recorded since Jan 1 and divided it by 365 days. The date on which this figure reached 60 µg/m³ was identified as the point when a city’s annual pollution allowance had effectively been exhausted.Delhi crossed this threshold within the first four months of 2026, followed by Bengaluru in late Sept and Kolkata in mid-Oct. Chennai and Mumbai were approaching the same benchmark when the analysis ended.For Kolkata, the timing is particularly worrying. The city typically sees its sharpest deterioration in air quality between Nov and Feb, when falling temperatures, weaker winds and reduced atmospheric mixing let pollutants accumulate closer to the ground.This means Kolkata has entered the winter pollution season having already accumulated enough PM10 to push its full-year average to the national limit.The findings also challenge the tendency to judge air quality primarily through daily AQI readings or exceptionally polluted winter days. articles.title: Convict on parole flees to Andaman, CCTV helps nab him
articles.summary: Life convict Arun Pandian fled parole to Andaman; CCTV at police station and phone records led Ramanathapuram police to track and arrest him.
articles.body: Madurai: A life convict from Tamil Nadu who absconded during parole flew to Andaman Islands, hoping to evade police and start a new life. But CCTV recording from a police station provided the crucial lead for Ramanathapuram police to unravel his escape plan, arrest him within days and return him to prison last week.Arun Pandian, 33, was serving life sentence at Madurai Central Prison when he secured 21 days’ parole last month for his mother’s eye surgery. He switched off his mobile phone and disappeared. When he failed to return to prison on Oct 2, police began searching but found no trace of him in Madurai, where his mother was undergoing treatment.The first breakthrough came when investigators reviewed CCTV footage from a local police station where Arun was required to report and sign during his parole under a court order. They noticed a man accompanying him during his visits. “Further investigation identified him as Arun’s friend Vinoth Kumar,” said Antony Raj, sub-inspector at Kenikarai police station in Ramanathapuram.Police then traced Vinoth’s mobile phone records, which revealed his journey from Madurai to Chennai and subsequently to Port Blair in the Andaman Islands. Vinoth had returned to Ramanathapuram, where police tracked him down. During questioning, he disclosed that Arun had sought his assistance, borrowed his phone and planned the escape to Andaman with his help.Ramanathapuram ASP K Nehaa subsequently contacted her IPS training batchmates E Kathiravan and Abhijeet Sirohi, who helped obtain passenger details of those arriving in Andaman after Oct 2. Investigators used the information to narrow down Arun’s whereabouts.Nehaa said Arun was staying at a friend’s house and had secured employment at a local bar for Rs 15,000. She said Antony Raj and his team travelled to Andaman and, with local police assistance, located and arrested Arun last week. articles.body: Trichy: Trichy Corporation has formed special teams for each of its five zones to address inundation complaints in residential areas during the northeast monsoon. Equipped with high-power diesel motor pumps, the teams are moving across the city to drain stagnant water and restore connectivity on affected roads.Corporation commissioner N Ponmani and mayor Mu Anbalagan inspected flood-prone areas in KK Nagar and Crawford on Sunday and directed ward-level officials to make use of the special teams.Officials said several parts of the city received 2-4cm of rainfall by Sunday morning, most of it on Saturday night. A team of workers has been assigned to divert rainwater to nearby drains and water bodies. As more properties have come up on vacant land, we had to intervene immediately to find alternatives for diverting stagnant water. articles.title: CM, NDA netas slam Kharge over remarks on PM’s father
articles.summary: Bihar NDA leaders, including CM Samrat Choudhary, demand Kharge and Rahul Gandhi apologise for ‘Modi ka baap’ remark at Patna event, calling it unacceptable.
articles.body: Patna: The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) netas in Bihar on Sunday hit out at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge over his “Modi ka baap bhi jayega” remark at a Patna event, calling it an attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s family and demanding an apology. CM Samrat Choudhary, Bihar BJP president Sanjay Saraogi and JD(U) state president Umesh Singh Kushwaha accused the Congress of lowering political standards and resorting to personal attacks amid its political setbacks.The CM demanded an immediate and unconditional apology from Kharge and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, describing the remark as “deeply unfortunate” and unacceptable in democratic politics.In a video statement released by the chief minister’s office, Choudhary accused the Congress leadership of targeting the Prime Minister’s family and said such language had no place in public discourse.“The statement made by Kharge is deeply unfortunate. Using derogatory language against PM’s father reflects the Congress’ and Rahul Gandhi’s hostility towards the his family. I demand that Kharge and Rahul immediately apologise for the offensive remarks against the PM’s father,” Choudhary said.He said political rivalry could not justify attacks on the family of the country’s PM. “The Congress party, its national president and its former president Rahul Gandhi must all apologise. Engaging in politics while showing such hostility towards the family of the country’s Prime Minister is unacceptable,” he said.Kharge made the remark while addressing a function in Patna marking the 139th birth anniversary of Bihar’s first chief minister Shri Krishna Sinha.
